items.title: Al Rose Interview, 1976-02-24
items.q: as Franco did it in Spain

ctx.x: So that the question of how, what new musical form may arise on the horizon doesn't interest you very much right now, because it's all speculation or it's all, it doesn't, it just hasn't come into existence yet. That's right. But politically, you seem to be very interested in change taking place in the culture. And maybe, I just wonder how you roll out.

Of course, my political attitude is a classical one in this sense. And that is that I believe that any true revolutionary socialist maintains his position on an entirely defensive basis. That is, that he assumes that the capitalist society in which we live is in a process of decline and inevitable collapse. I see the basic conflict as it exists in the world as one between capital and labor, which is certainly classical. I believe that there comes a time in the relations between capital and labor against the…
Now, New Orleans was a capitalist society at the turn of the century, or would you say?
